metadata.source: Ramchandra Pandeya: Madhyantavibhagashastram. Delhi : Motilal Banarsidass, 1971.

children.translated_text: Definition indeed is occlusion (<s>āvaraṇa</s>), the real nature (<s>tattva</s>), and the cultivation of the opponent’s antidote (<s>pratipakṣa-bhāvanā</s>)
Herein, the stages, the attainment of fruit, and the vehicles, and indeed the unsurpassed one as well
The non-existent construction (<s>abhūta-parikalpa</s>) exists; duality does not exist there

children.text: śūnyatā vidyate tvatra tasyāmapi sa vidyate // Mvk_1.2 //
children.translated_text: Emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) does exist there; and in that too, it exists

children.text: na śūnyaṃ nāpi cāśūnyaṃ tasmāt sarvaṃ vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: It is neither empty nor non-empty; therefore everything is established

children.text: sattvādasattvāt sattvācca madhyamā pratipacca sā // Mvk_1.3 //
children.translated_text: Because of existence, non-existence, and existence, that is the middle approach (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>)
An appearance of object, existence, self, and cognition arises
And cognition has no object; due to the absence of that, that too is unreal
Therefore its being a non-existent construction (<s>abhūta-parikalpatva</s>) is established
Not thus as total non-existence; liberation is accepted through the cessation of that
The imagined (<s>kalpita</s>), the other-dependent (<s>paratantra</s>), and the thoroughly established (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>) indeed
Are taught from the object, from non-existent construction, and from the absence of duality
Relying upon apprehension, non-apprehension arises
Not relying upon non-apprehension, non-apprehension arises
Therefore, from apprehension, the nature of non-apprehension is established
And from that, equality is to be understood between non-apprehension and apprehension
The non-existent construction (<s>abhūta-parikalpa</s>), and mental consciousness with its mental factors (<s>citta-caitta</s>) within the three realms (<s>tridhātu</s>)
Therein, the view of object is cognition; in the particularizations of that, the mental factors
Thus, conditioning cognition is one, and secondly the experiential (<s>upabhogika</s>)
There, the mental factors are the agents of delimitation of experience and of prompting
By covering, by implanting, and by leading, by appropriation
By filling, by the threefold delimitation, by enjoyment, and by exhausting
Through binding, through facing-towards (appropriative fixation), through affliction, the world is tormented

children.text: tredhā dvedhā ca saṃkleśaḥ saptadhābhūtakalpanāt // Mvk_1.12 //
children.translated_text: Defilement is threefold and twofold, and, due to non-existent construction, sevenfold

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ cātha paryāyastadartho bheda eva ca /
children.translated_text: And definition and synonym, its import, and distinction
And the means—thus emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is to be known in brief
The absence of duality; indeed the presence of absence—this is the mark of the empty

children.text: na bhāvo nāpi cābhāvao na pṛthaktvaikalakṣaṇam // Mvk_1.14 //
children.translated_text: Neither presence nor absence, not the characteristic of separateness or oneness
Thusness (<s>tathatā</s>), the limit of reality (<s>bhūta-koṭi</s>), the signless (<s>animitta</s>), the ultimate truth (<s>paramārthatā</s>)
And the <s>dharmadhātu</s>—these are synonyms of emptiness in brief
Unchangeableness, non-perversion, and the cessation of that—by the noble objects (<s>āryagocara</s>)
And because of being the causes of the noble qualities (<s>ārya-dharma</s>)—thus, in order, is the meaning of the synonyms

children.text: saṃkliṣṭā ca viśuddhā ca samalā nirmalā ca sā /
children.translated_text: It is defiled and it is pure, with stain and without stain
Purity is asserted like the purity of water, space, and gold
Emptiness of enjoyer, enjoyment, and the body thereof, and of the supporting thing

children.text: tacca yena yathā dṛṣṭaṃ yadarthaṃ tasya śūnyatā // Mvk_1.18 //
children.translated_text: And that—whatever and however it is seen, for that purpose—its emptiness
For the sake of attaining the twofold good (<s>śubha-dvaya</s>) and always for the welfare of beings
For the sake of abandoning <s>saṃsāra</s> and for the inexhaustibility of wholesome qualities (<s>kuśala</s>)
And for the purification of the spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>), for the obtaining of the marks and signs (<s>lakṣaṇa</s> and <s>vyañjana</s>)
For the purification of the Buddha-dharmas, the <s>bodhisattva</s> undertakes it
Here, emptiness is the non-existence of the person (<s>pudgala</s>) and of phenomena (<s>dharmāḥ</s>)
And the existence of that non-existence—therein that is the further emptiness
If it were defiled, then all embodied beings would not be liberated

children.text: viśuddhā cedbhavennāsau vyāyāmo niṣphalo bhavet // Mvk_1.22 //
children.translated_text: If it were pure, then striving would be fruitless

children.text: na kliṣṭā nāpi va 'ākliṣṭā śuddhāśuddhā na caiva sā /
children.translated_text: It is not defiled, nor is it undefiled; it is not pure, nor impure
Because of the luminosity of mind (<s>citta</s>) and because the affliction is adventitious

body.translated_text: Thus ends the first section on definition

children.translated_text: Pervasive, localized, excessive; taking up and avoiding
Twofold obstruction of duality is stated; ninefold is the mark of the defilements
The fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) are an obstruction to agitation and equanimity
And to the view of reality, to self-body view (<s>satkāya-dṛṣṭi</s>), and to that very entity
Regarding the jewels of cessation and path, there is gain and honor as well
In the understanding of affliction, and in the wholesome and so on, there is a further tenfold
Non-application in a non-sphere, and application undertaken in a wrong way
Non-arising, inattention (<s>amanaskāra</s>), and the non-fulfillment of the accumulation (<s>sambhāra</s>)
The despondency of spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>) and spiritual friend (<s>mitra</s>), the fatigue of mind (<s>citta</s>)
And the despondency of understanding (<s>pratipatti</s>), dwelling among ill-disposed people,
Roughness (coarseness), residual taint, and from the three—immaturity of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>)

children.text: prakṛtyā caiva dauṣṭhulyaṃ kausīdyaṃ ca pramāditā // Mvk_2.6 //
children.translated_text: And by nature indeed there is coarseness (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>), as well as sloth (<s>kausīdya</s>) and heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>)

children.text: saktirbhave ca bhoge ca līnacittatvameva ca /
children.translated_text: Attachment in becoming (<s>bhava</s>) and in enjoyments, and likewise mental sinking (<s>līna-cittatva</s>)
Lack of faith (<s>aśraddhā</s>), wrong resolve (<s>adhimukti</s>), and inquiry as words are heard (mere echoing of what is heard)
Lack of respect for the true Dharma (<s>saddharma</s>), and in gain, heaviness; likewise pitiableness (beggarliness)
Addiction to hearing (scriptural obsession) and paltriness, and inadequate preparation of meditative concentration (<s>samādhi</s>)
Wholesome (<s>śubha</s>), awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), undertaking (observance), intelligence, non-delusion, non-obstruction,
Fearlessness amid tumult (not trembling at crowds), absence of envy, mastery—such are the wholesome and the rest

children.text: trīṇi trīṇi ca eteṣāṃ jñeyānyāvaraṇāni hi /
children.translated_text: For these, the obstructions are to be known as three and three respectively,
While in the perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>) and the stages (<s>bhūmi</s>) on the side of the followers (<s>pakṣin</s>), there is yet another obstruction
Clumsiness with respect to the object, sloth regarding skill, and deficiency of the two kinds of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>)
Lack of superimposition (failure to imprint), or else weakness, and coarseness of view and badness of view
And there is a covering with respect to the lordly powers (<s>aiśvarya</s>) of the Well-Gone One (<s>Sugata</s>) and with respect to the giving up of beings,
And, concerning the decline and growth of faults, an obstruction in the bringing down (leading forth) of qualities
In release, in inexhaustibility, and in the uninterruptedness of the wholesome,
In the rendering-determinate (establishing as fixed), and in the maturation of the enjoyment of Dharma
In regard to the universally-pervasive aim, to the foremost aim, and to the foremost aim of outflow (emanation),

children.text: niṣparigrahatārtha ca santānābheda eva ca // Mvk_2.14 //
children.translated_text: And to the aim of non-acquisitiveness, and likewise to the non-dividedness of the streams (mental continua)
For the sake of untainted purity, and likewise for the aim of non-variegation (non-diversity),
And for the aim of neither loss nor excess, in the fourfold basis of mastery
In the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, this ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>)—unstained—is a tenfold covering,
And, as the counteragents by opposition to the ten stages (<s>daśa-bhūmi</s>), the stages themselves are the antidotes
The obstruction of defilements (<s>kleśa-āvaraṇa</s>) is declared, and likewise the obstruction with regard to what is to be known (<s>jñeya-āvaraṇa</s>),
Here, all obstructions—because of the exhaustion of which liberation is accepted

body.translated_text: Thus ends the Second Section on Obstructions (<s>Āvaraṇa-pariccheda</s>)

children.translated_text: Reality (<s>tattva</s>) of fundamental characteristics, and of the characteristic of non-perversion,
Reality consisting of result and cause, and both subtle and coarse
Established in common usage, with purity as its domain, graspable, with the mark of distinction,
And skillful reality, tenfold, in opposition to the view of self (<s>ātma-dṛṣṭi</s>)
The own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) is threefold; the unreal, and the permanent; and the real also, though not ultimately reality,
Thus, as real and unreal in respect of reality, the triple own-nature is accepted
Regarding imputation and rejection of both dharmas and persons (<s>dharma</s> and <s>pudgala</s>) here,
And the seeing of grasped and grasper (<s>grāhya</s> and <s>grāhaka</s>), and of existence and non-existence
That, from which cognition would not proceed—this indeed is the mark of reality,
For the unreal object has the characteristic of impermanence—arising and non-enduring
By the state of being impure and pure, in the root-reality in due order,
Suffering—called the mark of appropriation—is considered; another by connection
And non-existence is also the state of ‘not-that-existence’; the nature—emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is considered,
And the markless is non-self (<s>nairātmya</s>), and likewise that which is distinct from it
And the particular characteristic is specified—the truth of suffering is thus considered,
And habit-trace, and arising, and non-disjunction as well
The twofold origination of own-nature: the twofold defilement-and-pacification is considered,
In full knowing and in abandonment, and in attainment and direct realization are we
The truth of the path is declared, by designation and by actual practice,
And thus by bringing-forth it is noble; but ultimately, in one way only
By attainment of the aim and by reaching it, indeed the ultimate is considered as threefold,
And as twofold by reason of non-modification and non-perversion and thorough establishment
One, from common worldly convention; and, from three, what is established by reasoning,
The purified domain, in two ways, is proclaimed from just one
A dual inclusion of sign (<s>nimitta</s>) and conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), and of name (<s>nāman</s>),
And a single inclusion of right-knowledge and of true reality
The reality of activity is twofold: proper arrangement and bad arrangement,
One is the attainment of purity of characteristic and manifestation of cognition
Concerning single-causality, enjoyership, agency, subjection to control,
Regarding the meanings of lordship, permanence, and, even with the basis of purification from defilements
About yogic attainment (<s>yogitva</s>), about being bound and being freed, indeed the seeing of self (<s>ātma-darśana</s>) is to be understood here,

By the meaning of conceptual construction and de-construction (<s>parikalpa</s> and <s>vikalpa</s>), by the meaning of dharma-ness (thinghood) and object-meaning—therein, for those (cases), in those (contexts)
For the sake of delimitation by manifoldness and by summary from the outset,
And another (topic) is considered: the meaning of grasper and grasped (<s>grāhaka</s> and <s>grāhya</s>), and of the seed of that grasping
Another (topic), from the doorway of delimiting the object-to-be-known and of enjoyment,
Again, from superimposition and result, from striving and from non-superimposition and removal
Concerning the displeasing and the pleasing, and the purities: regarding co-arising and mastery,
Another (topic), by reason of attainment, of practice in accord (good conduct), and of dependence (other-power)
For the sake of apprehension, of the place, of the connecting, and of enjoyment; and for the sake of the twofold purity,
And another (topic) by reason of the use of result and cause, and also by reason of non-use
By the meaning of feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) and of sign (<s>nimitta</s>), and from the resorting to that sign,
Another is accepted by the joining with the meaning of its pacification and of its counter-agent
By cognition, free from discrimination of virtue and fault, externally and by itself,
Another knowable (topic) (is) from exit (going forth), along with designation (<s>sa-prajñapti</s>) and with causes

body.translated_text: From sign (<s>nimitta</s>), from pacification, from meaningfulness, the final (topic) is stated
Thus ends the Third Section on Reality (<s>Tattva-pariccheda</s>)
Fourth Section: On the Fruits of the Stages of Cultivating the Counteragents (<s>Pratipakṣa-bhāvanā-avasthā-phala-pariccheda</s>)

children.translated_text: Because of coarseness, because of being the cause of thirst (craving), because of being real (as object), and because of non-delusion,
For the entry into the Four Truths (<s>catuḥ-satya</s>), the cultivation of mindfulness-establishments (<s>smṛty-upasthāna</s>) (is taught)

children.text: parijñāte vipakṣe ca pratipakṣe ca sarvathā /
children.translated_text: When the contrary (fault) is fully known, and likewise the counteragent is fully (known),

children.text: tadapāyāya vīryaṃ hi caturdhā sampravartate // Mvk_4.2 //
children.translated_text: For the removal of that (fault), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) indeed is set in motion fourfold
Fitness for action, and stability therein, for the flourishing of all aims,
By the abandonment of five faults and by the application to eight cultivations (formations), in sequence
Laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), fault-finding talk (<s>avavāda</s>), stupefaction, sloth, excitation,

children.text: asaṃskāro 'tha saṃskāraḥ pañca doṣā ime matāḥ // Mvk_4.4 //
children.translated_text: Non-cultivation and cultivation—these five faults are considered
Support, and what is relied upon by it, its condition (occasion), and the fruit as well,
In regard to the object, non-bewilderment; and non-sloth and non-excitation; and recognition thereafter
The contriving for the removal of that (fault), in tranquility, is well-directed and well-conducted,
When the factor conducive to liberation is planted, by desire (<s>chanda</s>), application (<s>yoga</s>), and mastery (<s>adhipatya</s>)
In regard to the object, non-bewilderment, diffusion, and scrutiny as well,

children.text: vipakṣasya hi saṃlekhāt pūrvasya phalamuttaram // Mvk_4.7 //
children.translated_text: Since from the attenuation of the contrary (fault) the latter is the fruit of the former
Two and two are the factors partaking of penetration (<s>nirvedha-bhāgīya</s>), and the faculties (<s>indriya</s>) and the powers (<s>bala</s>) also,
The support-factor, the nature-factor, and the exit-factor are the third (set)
The fourth is the benefit-factor; the stainless-factor—these are regarded as threefold,
Here taught by cause and by support, and also by nature
And the analysis, then attainment, and other-assessment are threefold,
And the contrary and the counteragent—of the path these are the factors, eightfold then
In view, in discipline, and then in attenuation, the other’s ascertainment is admitted,
Being the flourishing of defilements and subsidiary defilements, and being the contrary and the counteragent
Favorable, perverted, and with accompaniment; the adverse (set),
And the non-perverted and perversion without accompaniment—this is the cultivation
By object and by attention, and by attainment, there is its specification,
Called the states of cause and the descents (entries), named as practice and fruit
Distinguished as what is to be done and what is not to be done, and higher and not-higher,

children.text: adhimuktau praveśe ca niryāṇe vyākṛtāvapi // Mvk_4.14 //
children.translated_text: In resolution (<s>adhimukti</s>) and in entry, and in exit, and even in prediction (<s>vyākṛti</s>)
In instruction, in consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), and in attainment, and in praising of benefits,

children.text: kṛtyānuṣṭhāna uddiṣṭā dharmādhātau tridhā punaḥ // Mvk_4.15 //
children.translated_text: The undertaking of the task is taught; again in the <s>dharmadhātu</s> threefold
Impure, pure-impure, pure, and thoroughly pure—according to reality,
The ordering of persons (<s>pudgala</s>) is thus considered according to what is appropriate
Receptacle-hood (<s>bhājanatva</s>), called maturation (<s>vipāka</s>), and strength by mastery of that,
Inclination, growth, and purification—this is the fruit in due order
Successively higher and the initial one, through practice, up to completion,
By favoring, and by the contrary, and, in particular, by disjunction

body.translated_text: And by being higher and not-higher, another fruit in summary
Thus ends the Fourth Section beginning with the Cultivation of Counteragents (<s>Pratipakṣa-bhāvanā</s>)
Fifth Section on the Supreme Vehicles (<s>Yānānuttarya-pariccheda</s>)

children.translated_text: Supremacy (<s>ānuttarya</s>)—in the attainment (resort) to it, again, is considered with respect to the object,

children.text: samudāgama uddiṣṭaṃ pratipattistu ṣaḍ vidhā // Mvk_5.1 //
children.translated_text: The coming together (convergence) is taught; but the practice is sixfold
In the highest right-attention, in the sub-dharmas, and in the exclusion of extremes,

children.text: viśiṣṭā cāviśiṣṭā ca paramā dvādaśātmikā // Mvk_5.2 //
children.translated_text: Distinguished and undistinguished, the supreme (practice) is of twelve aspects
Generosity of spirit, extensiveness of effort, the foundation, imperishability of nature,
Continuity, non-difficulty, expansiveness of resources, and appropriation—these are [the] factors // Mvk_5.3 //
Initiation, attainment, diffusion (outflow), and consummation are regarded as supreme,

children.text: tataśca paramārthena daśa pāramitā matāḥ // Mvk_5.4 //
children.translated_text: And thereafter, in the ultimate sense, the ten perfections (<s>Pāramitā</s>) are considered // Mvk_5.4 //

children.text: dānaṃ śīlaṃ kṣamā vīryaṃ dhyānaṃ prajñā upāyatā /
children.translated_text: Giving (<s>dāna</s>), discipline (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣamā</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), skill-in-means (<s>upāya</s>-ness),

children.text: praṇidhānaṃ balaṃ jñānametāḥ pāramitā daśa // Mvk_5.5 //
children.translated_text: Vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), power (<s>bala</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>)—these are the ten <s>Pāramitā</s>-s // Mvk_5.5 //
Assistance, non-obstruction, action (karma), and for that (action) forbearance (toleration),
Increase of qualities and capability, in descent (incarnation) and in emancipation // Mvk_5.6 //
Imperishability, constant functioning, fixedness in the ripening of enjoyments,
A mind-activity in accord with designation, of the <s>Dharma</s> of the Great Vehicle (<s>Mahāyāna</s>) // Mvk_5.7 //
For the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, continually, by threefold wisdom,
It is for the nourishing of the element (<s>dhātu</s>) by entries, and for the accomplishment of the aim // Mvk_5.8 //

children.text: saṃyuktā dharmacaritaiḥ sā jñeyā daśabhiḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Joined with Dharma-conducts, that (practice) is again to be understood by ten,

children.text: lekhanā pūjanā dānaṃ śravaṇaṃ vācanod grahaḥ // Mvk_5.9 //
children.translated_text: Writing, worship, giving, hearing, recitation, and taking up (retention), // Mvk_5.9 //
And proclamation, and self-study, reflection, and cultivation—this (is the ten),

children.text: ameyapuṇyaskandhaṃ hi caritaṃ tad daśātmakam // Mvk_5.10 //
children.translated_text: For that conduct, tenfold in aspect, is indeed an immeasurable mass of merit // Mvk_5.10 //
By distinction and by imperishability, and through benefiting others and by equanimity,
With non-distraction, non-perversion, reverence, and conformity with the Dharma // Mvk_5.11 //
Elation upon emergence, essence in regard to the object, and likewise the decline due to savoring and to attachment to abode,
Esteem and ulterior intention, and, even in attention, the conceit of ‘I’ // Mvk_5.12 //
A low-mindedness and distraction are to be discerned by the wise,
In attention to expression and to meaning, through non-diffusion with respect to the two characteristics // Mvk_5.13 //
In the impure and the pure, in adventitiousness, here fear and the uninclined (lack of aspiration),
From conjunction and from praise, and also from disjunction and from non-praise // Mvk_5.14 //
Existence and non-existence of the object in the expression—there is that non-perversion,
A twofold appearing, and likewise non-existence (of what appears) // Mvk_5.15 //
And in the object there is that non-perversion, being free from existence and non-existence,
Speech-activity conditioned by that discourse—an attention characterized by discursiveness, based upon that // Mvk_5.16 //
In attention there is non-perversion regarding the cause of the seeming of duality,
And the object’s non-existence like illusion (<s>māyā</s>) and its existence too—this is the view there // Mvk_5.17 //
That non-diffusion (composure) is non-perversion, because of non-diffusion regarding being and non-being,
The mere-named-ness of everything, for the cessation of all constructions // Mvk_5.18 //
Non-perversion regarding the specific characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>)—ultimately in the specific characteristic,

children.text: dharmadhātuvinirmukto yasmād dharmo na vidyate // Mvk_5.19 //
children.translated_text: Freed from the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, because a <s>Dharma</s> is not to be found // Mvk_5.19 //
Therefore in the general characteristic (<s>sāmānya-lakṣaṇa</s>) there is that non-perversion there,
Devoid of distorted and undistorted attentions, without decline // Mvk_5.20 //
Its impurity and purity—there is that non-perversion there,
Because of the purity of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, again by nature like space // Mvk_5.21 //
That the duality is adventitious—there is that non-perversion there,
For there is no defilement nor purification of dharmas and of persons (<s>pudgala</s>) // Mvk_5.22 //
Because of non-existence, fear, measure (conceit)—therefore there is that non-perversion here,
Inner plurality and unity also, even for the heretics and the disciples (<s>śrāvaka</s>) // Mvk_5.23 //
The limit of superimposition and of repudiation, twofold, concerning person and dharmas,
The limit of contrary and counteragent, termed eternalism and annihilationism // Mvk_5.24 //
In graspable and grasper, in defilement and in purification—twofold and threefold,

children.text: vikalpadvayatāntaśca sa ca saptavidho mataḥ // Mvk_5.25 //
children.translated_text: And the limit of the duality of conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>)—and that is considered sevenfold // Mvk_5.25 //
In being and non-being; in pacification, then in calming, in fear of that which is to be feared,

children.text: grāhyagrāhe 'tha samyaktvamithyātve vyāpṛtau na ca // Mvk_5.26 //
children.translated_text: In graspable and grasper; then in rightness and wrongness; and not in occupation (engagement) // Mvk_5.26 //
In non-arising and in co-temporality—there is that limit of the duality of conceptual construction,

children.text: viśiṣṭā cāviśiṣṭā ca jñeyā daśasu bhūmiṣu // Mvk_5.27 //
children.translated_text: To be known as distinguished and undistinguished on the ten <s>bhūmi</s>-s // Mvk_5.27 //
An order up to the limit, an element (<s>dhātu</s>), bearing of what is to be accomplished and of the means to accomplish,
A stream of determination and of predominance, penetration and diffusion // Mvk_5.28 //
Advance and well-orderedness, excellence—held as the object-support,
Non-deficiency, non-rejection, non-distraction, and fulfillment // Mvk_5.29 //
Arising and establishment, capability and non-establishment,
Unobstructedness, and for that, the advent of unrelaxing (unremitting) zeal // Mvk_5.30 //
The treatise is the Middle Division (<s>Madhyavibhāga</s>), and indeed with a meaning whose essence is profound and hidden,
And of great import, indeed of all import, and an incitement to the abandonment of all non-meaning (all that is not the aim) // Mvk_5.31 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the fifth chapter on the unsurpassed Vehicle (<s>yānānuttarya</s>) //
